2  JUDGMENT
This appeal by the claimant for enhancement, assailing the judgment and award in MVC No.682/2016 dated 08.01.2020 on the file of MACT, Humnabad.

The claimant suffered injuries on 03.07.2014 while riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-38/TD-1849 due to the rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-39/K-9696.
2.
The claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act before the Tribunal.

The claimant pleaded that he was working as coolie and aged 22 years and was earning Rs.20,000/-
per month at the time of accident.
It is further pleaded that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do any work.
3. After service of notice respondents No.1, 2 and 4 appeared through their counsels.
Respondent No3, though served, remained absent and was placed ex-parte.
Respondent No.2 its objections specifically disputed the accident.
Further contended that accident was due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by claimant himself.
He further denied the age, occupation and income of the claimant.
Respondent No.4 alleged that the accident was due to the negligent driving of the claimant himself.

4. The Tribunal on the bases of the pleadings, framed the following issues:
I. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the Motor vehicle accident occurred on 3-7-2014 at about 2.30 p.m on Chitguppa - Shamtabad road near Gunwant Hibare land, on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Honda Shine M/C vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-39/K-9696 and CBZ M/C bearing Temporary Reg. No.KA- 38/TD- 1849 bearing chassis No.MBLKC 14ABEGE06945 as alleged?
II.
Whether the petitioner further proves that he is entitled for compensation?

If so what is the quantum and from whom?
5.
The claimant examined himself as PW-1, examined one witness as PW-2 and marked Ex.P-1 to 54.

Respondents examined two witnesses as RW-1 and 2, marked Ex.R-1.
6.

The Tribunal taking into consideration evidence on record awarded compensation of Rs.7,63,514/- under various heads as under:
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3001-DB Sl. Compensation Different Heads No. Amount 1 Pain and suffering Rs.30,000/- 2 Medical Expenses Rs.1,28,714/- 3 Loss of future income Rs.6,04,800/-
Total Compensation Rs.7,63,514/-

3 The Tribunal directed respondents No.1 and 2 to pay the compensation jointly and severely.
The Tribunal fastened the liability 50% each on respondents No.1 and 2.
Respondents No.3 and 4, are owner and insurer of the motorcycle, on which the claimant was riding, though made as parties, no claim was made against them.

Hence, the Tribunal restricted the compensation to 50% against respondents No.1 and 2.
7.
The Tribunal while computing the compensation considered the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month, age of the claimant as 21 years and applied multiplier 18.

The Tribunal while assessing the disability considered the whole body disability at 40%.
8.

We have heard Sri.Babu H Metagudda, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri.Sudharshan M,
learned NC: 2024:KHC-K:3001-DB counsel for respondent No.2.
Notice to respondents No.1, 3 and 4 is dispensed with vide order dated 06.12.2022.
9. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that due to the accident, the claimant has suffered severe injuries.
The claimant is unable to attend his bodily needs or even walk without assistance.
It is further submitted that due to the accidental injuries, the claimant is not in a position to do any work and his functional disability is 100%.
The assessment of whole body disability at 40% as against 75% as assessed by doctor, who is examined as PW-2 and as per Ex.P-52, is incorrect and on the lower side.
10. Learned counsel further submitted that the accident was due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-39/K-9696.
He further submitted that the claimant was earning Rs.20,000/- per month as income.
It is further submitted that as per the medical evidence on record, the claimant would not be in a position to carry on his work as earlier and is deprived of his earning capacity.
The Tribunal committed an error in not awarding compensation towards future prospects.
Learned counsel further submitted that the Tribunal committed an error in not awarding any compensation towards loss of amenities, attendant charges and loss of earning during the laid up period.
Thus, prays to re-assess the compensation.
12. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer submits that the Tribunal is justified in holding that the claimant has contributed negligence to the extent of 50% to the accident.
The Tribunal is justified in considering the whole body disability at 40% on the basis of the evidence of PW-2/doctor.
PW-2 is not a treated doctor.
The assessment of disability by PW-2 is on the bases of medical records.
The Tribunal is justified in considering the whole body disability at 40% as against 75% as assessed by the doctor.
Learned counsel submits that the compensation awarded under various heads is just and reasonable.
Thus, prays to dismiss the appeal.

sentences.text: We have considered the submissions of learned counsels for the parties and perused the appeal papers.
The Tribunal on the bases of the evidence has recorded NC: 2024:KHC-K:3001-DB that the claimant while riding the motorcycle, owned by respondent No.3 has equally contributed to the accident.

Though, learned counsel for claimant contends that the claimant has not contributed any negligence to the accident, no evidence is placed on record or infirmity in the order of the Tribunal is pointed out to even prima facie demonstrate that the claimant has not contributed any negligence to the accident.
In the absence of any evidence on record, the finding recorded by the Tribunal regarding negligence does not call for any interference.
14. The claimant has contended that he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month by working as a labour.
No evidence is placed on record to prove the income or avocation.
In the absence of any evidence to prove the income of the claimant, the Tribunal is justified in assessing the notional income.
However, the notional income considered by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- per month is on the lower side.

As per the chart of KSLSA for the accidents occurred in the year 2014, the notional NC:
2024:KHC-K:3001-DB income is Rs.7,500/- per month.

We assert the income of the claimant at Rs.7,500/- p.m.
15.
PW-2/Doctor has clearly stated that due to the injuries, the claimant is unable to attend his own bodily needs without assistance of other person.
It is further submitted that he is unable to do his daily activities.
The doctor has stated that the claimant has suffered sequel of right FTP decompressive craniotomy due to which the disability would be at 75%.
Though, the insurer has extensively cross examined PW-2/doctor, no contrary evidence has been elicited.
Considering the nature of work and the loss of earning, the Tribunal committed an error in not awarding any compensation towards future prospects.
In view of the injuries, the claimant has suffered loss of earning.
Though, the claimant may carry on other activities, he will not be in a position to carry on his work as labour efficiently, as he was before the accident.

Hence, we hold that the claimant is entitled to future prospects at 40%, as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3001-DB Pranay Sethi, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, considering the age as 21 years and claimant is self employed,.

sentences.text: 16. Due to the accidental injuries and resultant disability, the claimant is unable to lead normal life and enjoy the amenities, which he would have enjoyed, but for the disability caused due to the accident.
The Tribunal committed an error in not awarding any compensation towards loss of amenities.
We hold that the claimant is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities.
17. The claimant has suffered severe injuries and was inpatient for 20 days.
In view of the nature of injuries and the treatment undergone, the compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and sufferings is on the lower side.
We enhance the same to Rs.60,000/-.

sentences.text: The claimant was inpatient for 20 days and was under the care of attendant.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation towards attendant and conveyance charges.
Considering the period of treatment, nature of injuries and the requirement of attendant, we award - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3001-DB compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards attendant and conveyance charges.
19. Considering that the claimant was inpatient for 20 days and would have been deprived from earning income, at least for a period of three months.
We award compensation of three assessed months income towards loss of earning during laid up period (Rs.7,500x3= Rs.22,500/-).

20. It is specifically contended by the learned counsel for claimant that due to the injuries suffered,
he is unable to continue his work as he was doing prior to the accident.
Due to the injuries, he is under constant care of the attendant.
The claimant is unable to do his day to day activities.
Apart from that, he has lost his earning capacity.
As per evidence of PW-2/doctor, the claimant cannot attend his work without assistance of other person.
He has suffered sequel of right FTP decompressive craniotomy, which would effect his professional as well as personal daily activities.

No contrary evidence is produced by the insurer or elicited while cross examining PW-2.
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3001-DB
When the doctor has assessed the disability at 75%, the Tribunal without any basis has considered only 40% as disability for computing compensation.

21. Considering the nature of work, disability, uncomfortness caused to the claimant and his inability to carry on the labour work as he was prior to the accident, the disability at 40% considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

It is settled position of law that while awarding compensation to the victim of accident, who is disabled either permanently or temporarily, not only the physical injuries, but his inability to live normal life and to perform his regular activities is also to be considered.
Further, the nature of work before the accident and the age of the victim is to be considered.
Due to the injuries, the claimant has been prevented or restricted from carrying on his professional activities.
If not all activities, at least to the extent of his regular activities for livelihood.
Considering the above aspects, we are of the view that, it would be appropriate to consider the functional disability at 60% for the purpose of awarding compensation.
He is - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3001-DB aged 21 years.
So, the multiplier is 18.
Hence, loss of future income comes to Rs.13,60,800/- (Rs.7,500 + 40% = Rs.10,500/- x 12 x 60% x 18).

22 . Thus, the total compensation of Rs.16,52,014/- is awarded as against Rs.7,63,514/-, under following heads:

- 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3001-DB ORDER
a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the MACT, Humnabad in MVC No.682/2016 is modified.
c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.16,52,014/- as against Rs.7,63,514/-.

d) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount along with interest @6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
e) Finding recorded by the Tribunal regarding negligence is sustained.
